title: “Some may feel law is moving in their direction”, says Govt spokesperson - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Cabinet Spokesperson Nalinda Jayatissa has stated that any decision on arrest or non-arrest will be based strictly on evidence uncovered during ongoing investigations, in remarks linked to the legal developments involving former President Gotabaya Rajapaksa.

“Arrest or non-arrest will be decided based on what is revealed during the investigation. As the investigation proceeds correctly, one might feel it is moving in their direction,” Jayatissa said, responding to reports that Gotabaya Rajapaksa had sought a court order to prevent a possible arrest under the Prevention of Terrorism Act.

He added that investigations will continue under established legal procedures, with outcomes determined by the findings of the inquiry.

title: Health system could face severe strain if Dengue cases continue to rise: Minister - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The healthcare system could come under severe pressure if the number of dengue patients continues to increase, Cabinet Spokesperson and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa warned today.

Speaking at the weekly Cabinet media briefing, Dr. Jayatissa said some hospitals, particularly in Colombo, are already experiencing overcrowding due to the growing number of dengue admissions.

“If patient numbers increase further, the hospital system may not be able to cope. We must reduce the number of infections,” he said.

The Minister stressed that preventing dengue transmission remains the most effective way to ease the burden on hospitals and healthcare workers. He urged the public to actively support ongoing dengue prevention programmes and eliminate mosquito breeding sites in their homes, schools, workplaces and surrounding environments.

Dr. Jayatissa noted that health authorities are closely monitoring the situation and have intensified dengue control activities in high-risk areas across the country.

He expressed confidence that the current rise in cases could be brought under control if the public fully cooperates with this week’s nationwide dengue prevention campaign.

title: Sri Lanka preparing contingency plans for potential El Niño impact - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Government is closely monitoring the anticipated El Niño climate phenomenon and is formulating plans to address its potential impacts, Cabinet Spokesman and Health Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said today (16).

Speaking at the weekly Cabinet media briefing, Dr. Jayatissa said several rounds of discussions have already been held under the patronage of President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to assess the possible effects of the weather pattern and prepare appropriate responses.

He noted that ministers have also discussed measures that can be implemented at the ministerial level to mitigate any challenges that may arise.

The Minister further stated that the Government is paying close attention to forecasts issued by the Department of Meteorology and is developing contingency plans based on weather conditions that could emerge over the coming year.

title: UN Resident Coordinator meets NCW Chairperson in Colombo - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The United Nations Resident Coordinator in Sri Lanka, Marc-André Franche, met with the newly appointed Chairperson of the National Commission on Women (NCW), Grace Asirwatham, at the Commission’s office in Colombo.

At the outset of the meeting, the Resident Coordinator congratulated the Chairperson on her appointment and reaffirmed the United Nations’ continued commitment to supporting the National Commission on Women in fulfilling its mandate under the Women Empowerment Act No. 37 of 2024. He was accompanied by representatives of UN Women Sri Lanka, while Commissioners of the NCW also participated in the discussions.

Welcoming the UN delegation, the Chairperson expressed appreciation for the ongoing support provided by the United Nations system, particularly through UN Women, in strengthening the operational capacity of the Commission. She noted the importance of technical assistance in developing institutional procedures, systems, and stakeholder engagement frameworks.

The Chairperson further outlined the key objectives of the Women Empowerment Act and highlighted the role of the National Commission on Women as an independent statutory body mandated to promote and protect the rights of women in Sri Lanka. She also briefed the delegation on progress made in establishing the Commission, including the development of governance structures, coordination mechanisms, and institutional capacity-building initiatives.

The Resident Coordinator reaffirmed the United Nations’ continued support for the operationalisation of the Commission and agreed to facilitate further engagement with relevant UN technical teams to explore areas of cooperation in priority areas.

The meeting concluded with a shared commitment to strengthening collaboration between the United Nations and the National Commission on Women in advancing women’s rights, promoting gender equality, and supporting women’s empowerment across Sri Lanka.

title: Seat belt rule on expressways to be strictly enforced from June 20 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The National Council for Road Safety has announced that the mandatory seat belt regulation on expressways will be strictly enforced from June 20, marking the end of the grace period granted to motorists.

According to Council Chairman Manjula Kularatne, all passengers travelling on expressways, including those seated in both the front and rear seats, must wear seat belts.

He stressed that no exceptions would be made once the grace period expires on June 19.

Authorities noted that while the regulation had already been introduced, enforcement was temporarily relaxed to give motorists time to adapt to the requirement.

title: Appeal Court to rule on Yoshitha’s revision plea on July 3 - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Court of Appeal today reserved July 3 for the delivery of its judgment on a revision application filed by Yoshitha Rajapaksa in connection with the money laundering case widely known as the “Menik Malla” case.

The application challenges a ruling of the Colombo High Court that rejected a preliminary objection raised by the defence during the trial proceedings.

The matter was taken up before a bench comprising Justices Amal Ranaraja and Sumudu Premachandra. Following the conclusion of oral submissions by both parties, the court fixed a date to announce its determination on the revision petition.

Rajapaksa has sought the Appeal Court’s intervention to set aside the High Court’s decision dismissing the preliminary objection, contending that the ruling warrants review by the higher court.

Counsel Hafeel Farisz appeared on behalf of the petitioner, while Senior Deputy Solicitor General Janaka Bandara represented the Attorney General.

title: Five arrested in Pulmuddai over alleged Rs. 20 Mn ancient rock deal - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - Five suspects who were allegedly preparing to sell a rock believed to be of ancient value for Rs. 20 million were arrested by Pulmuddai Police during a raid conducted in Pulmuddai.

The suspects, aged between 29 and 57, are residents of Puliyankulam, Eechchalanpattu and Trincomalee.

Police said the raid was carried out following a tip-off received by officers of the Pulmuddai Police Station.

However, the rock, believed to be of archaeological significance, was taken into police custody for further examination.

title: Fire at Karapitiya Hospital brought under control - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - A fire broke out at a transformer supplying power to the Cancer Unit of the Teaching Hospital Karapitiya around noon today (16), hospital officials said.

As a precautionary measure, hospital authorities immediately disconnected the electricity supply to the unit to ensure the safety of patients and staff.

The fire was swiftly brought under control through the joint efforts of hospital employees and the firefighting team of the Galle Municipal Council.

title: Cabinet nod to rebuild more religious sites damaged by Ditwah - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Cabinet of Ministers has approved funding to reconstruct an additional 90 places of worship damaged by Cyclone Ditwah, expanding ongoing efforts to restore religious sites affected by the disaster.

Official estimates show that 1,328 religious institutions sustained varying degrees of damage, including 758 Buddhist temples, 272 Hindu kovils, 199 mosques, and 99 churches.

Reconstruction work has already commenced at 178 religious sites through a Rs. 800 million fund mobilised by the Buddhasasana Fund, the Central Cultural Fund, and the Anagarika Dharmapala Foundation.

The allocation includes Rs. 200 million approved under a Cabinet decision on April 27, 2026.

The latest approval was granted following a proposal submitted by the Minister of Buddhasasana, Religious and Cultural Affairs to undertake restoration work at a further 90 places of worship from among the remaining affected sites.

title: Special Dengue prevention drive rolled out across all schools - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Ministry of Education has launched a special dengue control programme targeting all schools, preschools, and educational institutions across the country as part of the national effort to curb the spread of dengue.

In a circular issued to all provincial education authorities, the Ministry instructed institutions to identify and eliminate mosquito breeding sites based on several key risk factors.

The programme also calls for community-based clean-up campaigns and awareness initiatives to be carried out with the participation of students, teachers, parents, and local communities.

title: New causeway bridge planned across Angamuwa spill on Thambuththegama–Rajanganaya highway - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - A new causeway-type bridge will be constructed across the Angamuwa Spill on the Thambuththegama–Rajanganaya Highway to replace the existing box-culvert structure, following Cabinet approval for a major infrastructure upgrade aimed at improving connectivity and flood resilience.

The existing structure, located on the route linking the Anuradhapura–Padeniya and Anuradhapura–Puttalam highways, lies in a low-lying area and frequently becomes impassable during the rainy season due to flooding. Authorities have also identified that its current capacity is insufficient to meet future irrigation and water management demands in the region.

The proposed project will establish a new causeway-type bridge at the same location with enhanced capacity, supported through provisions of the Eppawala, Giribawa, Rajanganaya and Nochchiyagama Combined Water Supply Project implemented by the National Water Supply and Drainage Board.

The project is expected to strengthen transport reliability along the key highway network while also supporting long-term water management needs in surrounding agricultural and settlement areas.

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the proposal submitted jointly by the Minister of Transport, Highways and Urban Development and the Minister of Housing, Construction and Water Supply to implement the project at an estimated cost of Rs. 241.45 million.

title: Cabinet approves Badulla–Hali-Ela road rehabilitation using surplus loan funds - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Government has approved the rehabilitation and improvement of a section of the Badulla–Hali-Ela Road under the Peradeniya–Badulla–Chenkaladi Road (A05), utilizing surplus funds from an ongoing foreign-funded project.

The project for the improvement of the Badulla–Chenkaladi Road is jointly financed by the OPEC Fund for International Development (OFID) and the Saudi Fund for Development (SFD). A loan surplus of approximately USD 2.4 million has been identified from an associated road development project currently being implemented with Saudi Fund credit facilities for the Ampara–Uhana–Mahaoya Road.

With Cabinet approval granted for the reallocation, the surplus funds will be used to rehabilitate a 6 km stretch of the Badulla–Hali-Ela Road (from km 115 to km 121), which has been in use for over 15 years. The estimated cost of the project is Rs. 600 million.

The initiative will also include the reconstruction of a 1.5 km damaged section (from km 119+620 to km 121+200), which suffered severe damage due to Cyclone Ditva, according to authorities.

The proposal was submitted by the Minister of Transport, Highways, and Urban Development and received Cabinet approval as part of ongoing efforts to improve key national road infrastructure.

title: Rs. 1 billion allocated to modernize school hostels - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Cabinet has approved a project to modernize school hostel facilities across the country during the 2026–2028 period at an estimated cost of Rs. 1,008 million.

The decision was taken in response to concerns over the deteriorating condition of many school hostels, with authorities identifying 126 hostel buildings that are currently in an aged state and in need of urgent renovation and maintenance.

According to the Government, the limited maintenance carried out over the years has resulted in shortcomings in physical infrastructure, sanitation, health, and safety facilities, negatively affecting both the living conditions and academic performance of students residing in these hostels.

Recognizing the need to provide a more conducive environment for education and student well-being, the project aims to upgrade essential facilities and improve overall hostel standards.

The proposal was presented by Prime Minister and Minister of Education, Higher Education, and Vocational Education, and received Cabinet approval for implementation over the next three years.

title: Cabinet approves new National Action Plan to address human-elephant conflict - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The Cabinet of Ministers has approved a proposal to draft a new National Action Plan for Human-Elephant Conflict Management, as Sri Lanka continues to face a worsening crisis involving wild elephants and rural communities.

The proposal, presented by the Minister of Environment, comes amid a significant escalation of the conflict driven by population growth, expanding development activities, and widespread deforestation.

Cabinet Spokesman Nalinda Jayathissa said that these human-driven factors have led to the destruction of natural elephant habitats and the blocking of traditional migratory routes. As a result, the conflict has now spread across 19 of Sri Lanka’s 25 administrative districts, affecting 134 of the country’s 341 Divisional Secretariat divisions.

According to data from the 2024 wild elephant census, Sri Lanka’s elephant population is estimated at around 7,450. The ongoing human-elephant conflict continues to result in significant annual losses, including human and elephant deaths, as well as more than a thousand reported cases of property damage each year.

Although a National Action Plan to Mitigate Human-Elephant Conflict was introduced in 2020, the minister said that the situation has changed considerably in recent years, making the existing framework inadequate to address current challenges.

In view of this, the government has decided to move ahead with a revised and comprehensive national strategy aimed at more effectively managing the growing conflict.

title: Government names EPF-ETF study committee - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, June 16 (Daily Mirror) - The government  has approved the appointment of a Senior Officials Committee to examine the feasibility of bringing the operations of the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and the Employees' Trust Fund (ETF) under a single integrated governance framework managed by a tripartite board representing the Government, employers and employees.

The EPF, established under the Employees' Provident Fund Act No. 15 of 1958, currently serves more than 2.5 million members and manages assets exceeding Rs. 4.9 trillion. While the Central Bank of Sri Lanka is responsible for the fund’s custodianship, investment management, financial administration and payment of benefits, the Department of Labour oversees employer and employee registration, compliance enforcement, recovery of arrears and protection of employees’ rights under the Act.

The ETF, established under the Employees' Trust Fund Act No. 46 of 1980, operates under a tripartite board comprising representatives of employers and employees. The fund has an active membership of over 3 million and an asset base exceeding Rs. 637.5 billion.

According to the government, the tripartite governance model is an internationally recognised best practice in social security administration and is a key principle promoted by the International Labour Organization (ILO).

The proposal, presented by the Minister of Labour, seeks to assess the possibility of integrating the governance of both funds while ensuring stronger legal and financial safeguards for members' assets.

The Senior Officials Committee will study the proposal and submit recommendations on establishing a unified governance structure in line with international standards and best practices.
